title: Evaluation of a normalized derived comparison on successive resolutions
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal A',\mathcal B,\mathcal B'$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], and assume every complex in $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal A'$ admits a K-injective resolution (a quasi-isomorphism to a complex receiving only null-homotopic maps from acyclic complexes). Let $r:\mathcal A'\to\mathcal A$ and $s:\mathcal B'\to\mathcal B$ be exact additive functors, applied degreewise and descended to the ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $G:\mathcal A'\to\mathcal B'$ be additive functors [def-sp-left-exact-additive], with $Fr=sG$ on objects and morphisms. Let $RF,RG$ be their total right derived functors [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], with units $\eta^F,\eta^G$, and let
$$\beta:RF\circ r\xrightarrow{\sim}s\circ RG$$
be a supplied natural isomorphism. Suppose it is normalized as follows: for any K-injective $J$ in $\mathcal A'$ and any K-injective resolution $v:rJ\to T$ in $\mathcal A$, $Q_{\mathcal B}(Fv)$ is invertible and
$$(s\eta^G_J)^{-1}\circ\beta_{Q_{\mathcal A'}J}\circ(c^F_v)^{-1}=Q_{\mathcal B}(Fv)^{-1},$$
where $c^F_v:RF(Q_{\mathcal A}(rJ))\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{\mathcal B}(FT)$ is the canonical resolution identification [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation]; all exact-functor localization identifications are understood. Let $N$ be any complex in $\mathcal A'$, let $u:N\to J$ be a K-injective resolution, and let $v:rJ\to T$ be a K-injective resolution. Put $w=v\circ r(u):rN\to T$, another K-injective resolution since $r$ is exact. Under the resolution identifications $c^F_w$ and $s(c^G_u)$ of [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation], the comparison at $N$ is
$$s(c^G_u)\circ\beta_{Q_{\mathcal A'}N}\circ(c^F_w)^{-1}=Q_{\mathcal B}(Fv)^{-1}:Q_{\mathcal B}(FT)\longrightarrow Q_{\mathcal B}(F(rJ))=Q_{\mathcal B}(sGJ).$$
The equality is valid for every such $u,v$, with the canonical changes of resolution in [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation]; it does not assume that $rJ$ is K-injective.
